reasons: Default secret key is a placeholder and must be changed.
The settings file shows a default for some values that the environment template also sets, so the two can disagree.

terms.meaning: A named value that the operating system passes to running programs.
A library that checks that each setting has the right type.
A single shared record of all the app's settings.
Saving a result so it is not recalculated each time it is asked for.
A switch that turns a feature on or off.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file header
sections.what: Names the file and imports the tools used to define the settings.
sections.why: Needed so the settings can be read and checked.

sections.name: Settings (part 1)
sections.title: Core app and database settings
sections.what: Defines the basic app name, environment name, log level, debug switch, database address and database password default, the cache address, and the security settings for tokens.
sections.why: These values control how the app runs and connects to its database.
sections.watch_out: The default secret key is a placeholder. The app will run with it unless it is changed.

sections.name: Settings (part 2)
sections.title: AI provider and external service settings
sections.what: Defines the keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Cohere and Hugging Face, the default provider and model, the embedding model, the local model addresses, and the Qualtrics survey service details.
sections.why: Lets the app pick which AI service to use and how to reach it.
sections.watch_out: The default provider is set to OpenAI, so an app without an OpenAI key fails on first AI request.

sections.name: get_settings
sections.title: Settings file loading and shared object
sections.what: Defines the settings file name and rules, including ignoring unknown variables, and provides a cached helper that creates the settings object once. A shared settings object is created when the file is first loaded.
sections.why: Creating the settings once keeps every part of the app reading the same values.
sections.watch_out: Because the shared object is created on import, a missing DATABASE_URL stops any file that imports settings, not only the app start.

summary: Reads all app settings from the environment file and from the system, checks their types, and provides one shared settings object for the rest of the app.
purpose: Gives the app one place to get its settings so they are not scattered through the code.
why: Likely reason: keys, addresses and switches change between computers, so they are read from the environment rather than written in the code.
how: It defines a Settings class listing each setting with its type and default value. The settings are read from the environment file, with names matched without case sensitivity. A cached helper creates the settings once, and a shared settings object is created when the file is loaded.
inputs: The environment file and system environment variables, such as DATABASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY.
outputs: A settings object used by the database, the API, and the services.
risks: DATABASE_URL has no default, so the app will not start without it. The default secret key is weak. The settings object is created as soon as this file loads, so a bad setting stops the app early.
debug: If the app will not start with a settings error, check that DATABASE_URL is set in the environment file. If a value is ignored, check its spelling and that it is in the environment file. To see the loaded values, print the settings object.
